verdict.description: What happens to this PR, and nothing else: none of the four ends the day and none of them waits for anybody. pass and pass_with_followup merge it. hold leaves the PR open and returns the card to the pool with the reasons on it. ask leaves the PR open and sends the card to `pending` tagged `regrill`, carrying the decision nobody here could make. No second field says the same: two fields for one decision can contradict each other, and the day would obey the wrong one.

audited_head_sha.description: The SHA actually read, taken from the PR and never from the handoff. If it disagrees with the worker's, the day stops: the verdict would be about different code than was delivered.

reasons.description: Why this verdict and not another. One reason per entry, one sentence each, naming its evidence — the PR comment renders these as one line apiece. What the task asked for and the diff does not carry goes here.

unreported_decisions.description: Decisions visible in the diff or the PR that the worker did not declare. The central finding of this audit, and a field of its own for that reason: in prose it gets buried, which is the problem it came to solve.

found_in.description: File and line, or where in the PR.

invalidates_diff.description: True if resolving it the other way would pull down what was pushed. Decided by reading the diff, not by copying the worker's blocks_the_pr.

isc_unproved.description: Claims marked [x] whose probe could not be corroborated with independent evidence.

actions_taken.description: What was actually done: comments, cards, tasks put back to Open. It is what the user reads in the morning.

decisions_owed.description: Only when the outcome or verdict says a decision is owed, and empty otherwise. Each one goes onto the card in writing and the card goes to `pending` with the `regrill` tag: nobody is interrupted, and a grill settles it before any session touches the card again. The bar is that the answer changes what the person using the app experiences, not how the code gets there.

what.description: The decision, in one sentence, named the way somebody who has not read the code would name it. This is what a grill reads first, so it is the one field nothing may leave out.

why.description: What is different depending on the answer, in one sentence.

options.description: The answers you can see on offer, if you can see them. Two or more, or none at all -- one option is not a decision. A grill may find others; this is what saves it the rediscovery.

card.description: Where this card goes when the PR is not merged, and what it carries. Only read on `hold` -- `pass` merges and `ask` always goes to `pending`. Omit it to let the day decide, which sends the card back to the pool the first time and to `pending` the second. The orchestrator does the moving; naming it here is what makes the destination a reading of the PR rather than a default.

to.description: `Open` puts it back in the pool for the next session. `pending` waits on a person. A card already returned once goes to `pending` whatever this says: two sessions that could not land it is a person's problem, not another session's.

tags.description: Tags to add on the way. `regrill` is the one that matters: it says the hold is not about this diff but about a question the card never settled, so a grill has to reach it before another session builds the same thing again.
